The authority being not satisfied with the explanation of the petitioner appointed one Obaidul Haq, Assistant Director of the Directorate as inquiry officer to enquire into the allegation against the petitioner. The enquiry officer after holding enquiry submitted his enquiry report though he conducted the enquiry without following some mandatory provisions of law as provided in the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1985. Thereafter, the authority issued second show cause notice to the petitioner vide Memo Nathi No.2 Shanstha-23/(14) PL/I and 184/3817 dated 21-11-1991 without enclosing the enquiry report in full. The petitioner replied to the second show cause notice by his letter dated 17-12-91 denying all allegations explaining his defence. But unfortunately, the authority paying no heed to that explanation did not pass any final order to the aforesaid departmental proceeding against the petitioner and since no final order was passed on the aforesaid departmental proceeding the petitioner was compelled to file Writ Petition No.4470 of 1996 before this court against the respondents and this court was pleased to issue Rule on 3-11-96 in which a direction was given to complete the departmental proceeding started against the petitioner by passing final order within two months and while the said Writ Petition was pending for disposal on the selfsame allegation as stated above, Ramma Police Station Case No.31 (6)93 was started against the petitioner and the said case was quashed by the High Court Division by the judgment and order dated 9-2-95 in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.799 of 1994. 

 8. Mr SAM Mahbub Elahi, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the respondents, on the other hand, opposes the Rule raising a preliminary point on the ground of maintainability of these Writ Petitions and contended that the Writ petitions are not maintainable in its present form as the matter involving in the writ petitions are the subject matter to be decided by the Administrative Tribunal under Article 117(2) of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. He has further submitted that the present case involves the question of the departmental proceedings which is very much within the jurisdiction of the Administrative Tribunal. 

 11. It is now settled by our apex court that matters relating to or arising out of the terms and conditions of the persons in the service of the Republic should be adjudicated by the Administrative Tribunal exclusively. In a number of decisions our apex court decided this issue which is no longer res integral. In the case of Mujibur Rahman (Md) vs Government of Bangladesh 44 DLR (AD) 111 it was decided, within its jurisdiction the Tribunal can strike down an order for violation of principle of natural justice as well as for infringement of fundamental rights, guaranteed by the Constitution, or any other law. A person in the service of the Republic who intends to invoke fundamental right for challenging the vires of a law will seek his remedy under Article 102(1) but, in all other cases, he will be required to seek remedy under Article 117(2). 

 Reflection of the above decisions are also to be found in the case of SP Sampad vs Union of India AIR 1987 (SC) 385, JB Chopor vs Union of India, AIR 1987 page 357 and so many other decisions. Fortified with these decisions, we are of the view that the petitioner in the present case who is a government servant can always ventilate his grievance before the Administrative Tribunal as constituted under Article 117(2) of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh if he is so advised.
